clipTools.reason: Core 0.1.56's pilot launcher builds the API environment only from config.json keys and has no setting for CLIP_FFMPEG_PATH, CLIP_FFPROBE_PATH or CLIP_RASTERIZER_PATH (providerCredentials only accepts API key names), so there is no supported way to pass them; editing the installed runtime was not done
clipTools.effect: the media page still says the clip tools are not set up; exact clips and frame checks are unavailable on the pilot
clipTools.followUp: Core change needed: a pilot config key for the clip tool paths

pilotAcceptance.harness: verification/pilot-acceptance.mjs from the local 0.1.56 acceptance worktree (course main e6aa1be + local 0.1.56 pin commit a0f8d5e; pilot-acceptance.mjs unchanged since 0.1.47), run as a guarded copy
pilotAcceptance.noProviderGuard: AI services are on with the owner's real key, so the run used a copy with two added stops: abort if the QA account has no enrollment (enrolling emits a supervised event) and abort if the first episode is not already completed (answering checks or completing an episode emits supervised events). Neither stop fired. Session-end signals (new in 0.1.56) start supervisor work only with the learner's supervision opt-in, which the QA enrollment does not have, and the session.ended event itself is not supervised
skippedSteps: answering the first episode's checks and completing it (already completed; the guard would have stopped the run)
admin signed-in checks (no operator password; the admin sign-in page was checked signed out)

pilotAcceptance.writesByDesign: the harness sets a fresh random password for the dedicated QA account through the runtime's set-password CLI (never printed or stored), signs that account in, and writes its receipt and screenshots to the pilot's acceptance folder
